entry.title: THE FERDAWS SQUARE
entry.summary: 2003: After Saddam's Fall in 2023 a group of artists, intellectuals, and activists started a bus trip to Baghdad to Firdaws Square. We…
entry.content: 2003: After Saddam's Fall in 2023 a group of artists, intellectuals, and activists started a bus trip to Baghdad to Firdaws Square. We went by coach during the day; we reached Firdaws Square. There was the famous sculpture of Saddam that was destroyed during the opening of Baghdad; the American soldiers were everywhere, and the surroundings of the place were full of tension, even though we were young and weren't aware of the complications of the situation. But in the place which, for most of us, was the first time to see or to visit, it was something strange because we were following the news on an hourly basis and the place was familiar on TV, but that image becoming real was a strange realisation. But we knew later that the reality of the place was also the surface of what was happening, but still we laid down a big canvas on the floor and started to paint as a way to say we are building the same imagination for the future Iraq, and we started to paint as well on the remains of the sculpture; the children who were around were also invited to paint the canvas with us. Even one of the artists later told us that they took inspiration from this event to build a sculpture on top of the place in a freer, more modernised style to show that the future of art in Iraq will change from building multiple images of Saddam to a new art environment that provides freedom to individuals and freedom of expression, which, of course, during Saddam's time, every aspect of art was observed and monitored harshly; of course, later even the sculpture was removed from the place.

entry.title: DWAROZH CENTRE
entry.summary: Photo by: Sami Moumin 2002, I was visiting the Dwarozh Centre, which was a centre for education and activities targeted toward the younger…
entry.content:
2002, I was visiting the Dwarozh Centre, which was a centre for education and activities targeted toward the younger generation, connecting to other groups of intellectuals. Many of today's known personalities were visiting the place.
Madhat Kakei, the Kurdish artist who was a pioneer for the young and our generation, started a workshop with some of us who were just in the final years of college; the workshop didn't end up with an exhibition but was a great exchange of experiences on painting. After the workshop, there was a big room that was left over for construction to take place. I decided with the director to use the place for some time as an installation space, even though at the time my knowledge were very limited about installation and other forms of art outside painting; that's why I stared to collect as many cartons as possible to build an installation and to start painting on them and hanging them to the room until it was completely covered, with some parts being treated as internal sculpture to treat it as a play that the place is not just walls but an atmosphere to move inside.

entry.title: GWRIS (Rope) گوریس
entry.summary: 2010 Gwris (Rope) is a collaborative work with older generation in the Delezha Village,  who still had the skill to make it, there…
entry.content: 2010 Gwris (Rope) is a collaborative work with older generation in the Delezha Village,  who still had the skill to make it, there was a twist, in which I told them can you make me the beigest Gwris, I provided materials whish is a normal fibre made goats hair that used to make roap, the Technik is not so complicated but at least need a steady hand and some experiences to make which younger generation without you tube tutorials cant do it. The event of making it became an occasion in the village; all the older generation gathered around and participated and the result was a 14-metre-long rope that I showed in the installation inside Goldsmiths' Final Show, to make a big swing facing the Video Dropping; people were swinging and seeing the video on the wall.

entry.title: BECOMING A DOG
entry.summary: 2013 The process of the work started from a second-hand market near Goldsmith College when I bout an album for one pound; it…
entry.content:
2013 The process of the work started from a second-hand market near Goldsmith College when I bout an album for one pound; it looked nice and old-style. My surprise was it was full of pictures, and when I asked about the pictures, they said it was free; you could throw it away. Then the Idea of turning this material that has zero value into an experience and a little discovery, and maybe give it value through making it into artwork that has value to others. The research happened when there was no AI to give the picture to and analyse the symbols; then I had to go through the pictures one by one, finding symbols and places that are possible to visit. The closest place I found in the picture was a castle called  Hampton Court Palace.

How to find the places name and when it located it needed many days of comparation between  pictures of palaces in UK to find the perfect match and while the the family had a visit to the side the two couple and a son aged between 15 to 20 probably, and a dog, I wanted to visit the site but while the visiting new places gives you exciting interest for new palace or things to see, this excitement all has gone through thousand pictures of the place of every corner, every inch. Then I thought seeing the place as a human who builds a very complicated system of images that kills the feeling of new experiences is not possible. 

I started thinking what the experience would be if I visited as a dog that was in the pictures. From this perspective, I attached a Handycam to my head and visited the place, walking on my knees and hands to position my head in the dog's place. The first show of the whole work as an installation was inside my studio for the visiting tutors. I filled a wall with pictures of the place, and the video I recorded with the camera also had to be edited to look like the dog's vision; the video had to become square, with the possibilities that dogs see 290 angles instead of humans' 180 angles and reduced to the colours the dog sees.  I tried to get as much out of the materials as possible, like I did a little animation to get the album ready for research and artwork, but it was never fully ready for exhibition on its own in London.

2017 The Workshop at Silemany University.

When the University of Silemani asked me to do a seminar in the College, I thought it would be better to do a workshop for students that motivates them to understand both the curating process and to build their own work from unknown materials that are new to them. After the materials were used to make their own exhibition. I gave my seminar on the day of the exhibition to show that there are various viewpoints for the same material.

entry.title: CIGARETTE FILTER
entry.summary: 2013 Cigarette filter, Video 56 seconds looping.  The work is a collection of more than one year's worth of photos of cigarette filters…
entry.content:
2013 Cigarette filter, Video 56 seconds looping. 

The work is a collection of more than one year's worth of photos of cigarette filters in different locations, starting from Sulaymaniyah to London; later, it was all brought together in one video. The work was exhibited in many places, starting with the first-year MFA Fine Art student show at Goldsmiths, London. 

The work later became part of the Project Xashak exhibition, which I curated.  Inside the old Cigarette factory, in order to support the transition of the place to become today's Culture Factory ( the biggest cultural project in Iraq).
This was the first exhibition inside the Culture Factory, and the start of the long relationship with the place that many projects and artworks produced some in reaction or critical respond to the crises inside the factory and some others as support for establishing supporting circle to protect the creative transition of the place, the work tuning body was produced there with a series of works that were my project to work on the place from a critical aspect.

entry.title: MY RELATIONSHIP WITH THE PICKUP
entry.summary: 2008 My relationship with the pickup, photo documentation of an action.  The work is part of the ( City Project ), which was…
entry.content:
2008 My relationship with the pickup, photo documentation of an action. 

The work is part of the ( City Project ), which was a project that started as a Curatorial collaboration between Shirwan Xan, Sherko Abbas and Rebeen Hamarafiq ( myself ) under the name of the organization Art Art Labour.

Artists: Avan Omar, Rozhgar Mustafa, Nahro Shawqy, Hamn Hameed, Gaylan Abdulla, Rebeen Hamarafiq, Sakar Sleman, Aram Ali, Poshya Kakl، Narmeen Mustafa . 

The Idea was to work inside the city as a medium instead of concentrating on the result to be shown in a gallery space, but rather a series of actions happening in the time and spaces of the city, which at the time happened between Sulaymaniyah and Erbil. 
This work was a record of a daily route between my house and the Directory of publishing house whish was my job place. every day there was a little twist depending on the the relation that happened to establish between me and this Pickup who were parking at the same place everyday. but according to his mood, my route hade to make a little change, if the driver had the mood to park perfectly, then I had to walk extra few metres and go around the pickup; some days he wasn't parking perfectly, then I had space to walk between the pickup and the wall. The little extra metres were a minor problem in general, but the work wanted to show that every object in the city have relation with our lives on a daily basis, and we are in continuous relation with every aspect inside our cities.

entry.title: Ladybug, ladybug, where is my uncle's house.
entry.summary: Ladybug, ladybug, where is my uncle's house 2016 Ladybug, ladybug, where is my uncle's house. خاڵخاڵۆکە ماڵی خاڵم لە کوێیە The work is…
entry.content:
2016 Ladybug, ladybug, where is my uncle's house.
خاڵخاڵۆکە ماڵی خاڵم لە کوێیە

The work is a performance or an action during the teachers' strike, while all the participants were shouting Where is our salary out loud. I started to repeatedly tell Ladybug, " Ladybug, where is my uncle's house.  ( خاڵخاڵۆکە ماڵی خاڵم لە کوێیە ) A Kurdish riddle made as an illusion for kids: when they capture the Ladybug, they will sing the riddle, and the illusion is that the Ladybug will travel in the direction of one's uncle's house. Even the original song's words build illusory, performative power leading to action. During this performance, even the song was sung for a plastic ladybug, which reduces performativity from the riddle completely.

Documentation; Rozhgar Mustafa.

entry.title: 2009 - 2012 Free Watermelon
entry.summary: 2012, More Utopia, Performance, London.  The performance took place inside Goldsmiths, London, when the history of the work started to allocate around other…
entry.content:
2012, More Utopia, Performance, London. 

The performance took place inside Goldsmiths, London, when the history of the work started to allocate around other discourses on the history of the use of watermelon and connecting it to Black and African colonialism, imagining others as free savages. Then the watermelon performance this time was performed in front of audiences with less preparation than the original performance in 2009. And this time the artist Sherko Abbas accompanied me and documented the performance. 

2009 Eat watermelon for free, Westfield, London.

In the same year, for the first time, I had a one-month residency in London with the organisation Art Role, Artsadmin, Live Art Development Agency. During the residency the artists from Live Art Agency sent letters as guidance for making public works in London, and during the residency I prepared one performance with the work watermelon but this time instead me eating it I cut it in circles and put them on a table in front the newly opened Westfield in London and Asked out loudly eat watermelon for free but the rule was no one had the right to cut the watermelon they had to eat it from the middle while the work was a struggle between desire and body boundaries, social norms and of course my elementary-level English and other politics regarding public space, because during the little time of the performance three time the security came to us asked us to leave as we were advised after the third time the, we had to leave because they had the right to take us to the police station. During the performance, the artist, Shabnam Shahbazi, accompanied me, documenting and helping. 

2009 Going back to nature, Kanysard, Silemany.

: Going Back to Nature was the name of a TV program broadcast by Kurdsat TV and was hosted by the artist Esmail Hhh. The nature of the program was to take the artists to nature and record their painting of nature how realistically they paint nature, some in their style but converted to painting a nature that can be seen by camera and also then recording how the artist turns it to a painting, a drawing, watercolour, and other artistic materials. I remember criticising it on many occasions that this type of program reduces the imagination of normal people to the level that art is one style of painting, and that is realistic depiction of nature. The director of the program was a friend of mine; he once met me and said Why do you come to put your style in nature with the program, and I said If I come, my artwork won't be painting. " He said, " I promise whatever you did, we will include it in the program and will be broad casted.

As a challenge to the program and the Idea of one-directional imagination of art, I accepted and brought one watermelon to the program. During the day, I announced to the artist that I would now do a performance with the Idea of going back to nature. I started to cut the watermelon in half with a sharp stone and started to eat it without cutting it into more pieces. The audience were the artists who thought they were doing the best method of painting what they saw, because the director at Kurdsat TV never agreed to put the performance in the actual TV program.

entry.title: 2017, 2019 Running Around Cigarette Factory
entry.summary: Running Around Cigarette Factory 2017, 2019. The work started when, at the beginning of the transformation of the old Cigarette Factory into the…
entry.content:
Running Around Cigarette Factory 2017, 2019. The work started when, at the beginning of the transformation of the old Cigarette Factory into the new Culture Factory, many groups who were claiming and fighting for the place started to publish their project for the place in social media. In contrast, as the fight started to be directed toward social media, I prepared a participatory performance. I invited everyone to have a walk and a run around the factory, just to make it clear that the factory, 76,000 square metres in the middle of the city, is big enough to accommodate all activities in the city, not just a few groups. Mhamad Nakam, a young and interesting storyteller. wrote a short story, and the story was divided into 17 cards and spread across five places for the walkers to collect during the walk. By the end, because there were 17 cards and each person collected only 5, they had to share their card with others in order to re-make the story.

in 2019 the Material of the first performance was installed and made open to public and this time I invited audiences to re-invent part of a story written on 17 small carts.

entry.title: Fresh Almonds from Ser Marya los Spain 2013 - 2014
entry.summary: During the residency at Joya: Art + Ecologia Rebeen noticed that the almond trees are left with many fresh green almonds. This was…
entry.content:
During the residency at Joya: Art + Ecologia Rebeen noticed that the almond trees are left with many fresh green almonds. This was a surprise because in his home country, the fresh green almond is one of the most beloved foods; through more research and questions, many layers were revealed, showcasing different politics behind the leftover almonds. Linking neoliberalism to the transformation of the almond industry from Spain to California. The dream of making Spain the world's main almond producer, and some ecological catastrophes: replanting large farms with almond trees instead of naturally varied trees, with almond trees imported from Syria, most likely from the Kurdish region. How the big farms were evacuated after the shift to almond production in the USA; then the farms couldn't survive the price competition, so they were left as they were.

The collected almonds were brought back to London because nobody had a desire to eat the fresh green almonds; then it was spread among the Kurdish Families who were living there, some of them were away from this nostalgic taste for decades. The aim was to make them feel at home, even for a few seconds, while the whole context gives another dimension: the politics that connect the world together. 

2013 The packages got ready to be sent in London and examples the seminar in Camberwel College London.
